blocks.text: IRMAA — What It Is and When It Applies

IRMAA (Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount) is a Medicare surcharge added to Part B and Part D premiums when household MAGI exceeds thresholds. It uses a two-year lookback — 2027 premiums are based on 2025 income, 2028 on 2026, and so on. MAGI includes tax-exempt interest. Brad turns 65 in June 2027 and Lisa in November 2027; Brad can likely delay Part B while covered by Oracle's plan. Retirement is expected at 66–67 (not yet set), so a retirement-year income appeal would apply to a later year than 2027.
IRMAA Thresholds (2026 — MFJ)

Part B figures are per person (2026). Tier 4 and Part D amounts: confirm on Medicare.gov. Thresholds adjust annually; 2027 values are projections only. Brad's 2025 MFJ AGI of $337,561 falls in Tier 2 — plus any tax-exempt interest.

blocks.text: RMDs — Required Minimum Distributions

RMDs begin at age 75 for anyone born 1960 or later — 2037 for Brad (born 1962). Lisa's start year follows her birth year; confirm. The IRS requires minimum annual withdrawals from Traditional IRAs and 401ks. Roth IRAs and HSAs have NO RMDs. The amount equals the prior year-end balance divided by an IRS life-expectancy factor.
